metadata.title: Upwork Overhaul Plan: Aryan P. (Top Rated, 100% JSS)

how_the_data_was_collected.item: Profile, My Stats and Proposals pages read on 2026-10-04 through the logged-in Chrome session.
Live job-market numbers taken on 2026-10-04 from Upwork job search and Project Catalog search in the same session (payment-verified clients, sorted by newest).
External evidence from Upwork's own research and help pages plus third-party pricing and digital-product sales data. Every source is listed in the sources section.

metadata.reading_guide: Each claim is tagged as one of three kinds. "observed" means read directly from Upwork on 2026-10-04. "cited" means taken from a named external source. "assumption" means a planning estimate of mine that you must test; it is not proof.

executive_summary.finding: The profile has strong trust assets (Top Rated, 100% Job Success, 35 jobs, 20K+ USD earned) but the sales funnel is switched off: 0 proposals sent in the last 3 months, 0 profile views in the last 7 days, availability badge off, 12-month earnings of 2,172 USD. The problem is activity and positioning, not reputation.

The profile and catalog are aimed at thin demand. "OpenClaw" returns 24 jobs across roughly two quarters, mostly under 1,000 USD. Jobs with "Claude" in the title number 300 to 350 open postings, about 10 new per day. Reposition around Claude implementation (Claude Code, Cowork, skills, MCP connectors) for businesses.

Premium AI jobs are crowded: most reach 20 to 50 or 50+ proposals within 2 to 5 days. The low-competition pockets are setup, training, coaching, audits and tool-specific integrations, often posted by clients with 40K to 400K+ USD lifetime spend. That is exactly where a done-for-you offer fits.

The done-for-you line is where the money is. The do-it-yourself pack is worth building, but the sales data says most packs earn very little without an audience (median listed skill earns under 50 USD per month). Build the pack once as your delivery toolkit and credibility asset, and treat its direct sales as a bonus.

Your 100% Job Success Score rests on a small recent base (about 2K USD in 12 months), and Upwork weights higher-earning jobs more heavily. One bad outcome on a large contract would move the score a lot. The plan therefore starts every new client with a small paid first milestone.
executive_summary.honest_expectation: Signing and funding a first contract inside 7 days is realistic. Cash in your bank inside 7 days is not, because of Upwork's payment holds (see first_week_cash_reality). "Huge money" in week one is not supported by any evidence I found; a realistic first-month target is in the targets section and is labelled as an assumption.

problem.what: The funnel is off. No proposals, no badge, no views.
problem.fix: Turn on the availability badge, reply to the open invite, and start the daily proposal routine in mcp_operating_system.

problem.what: Rate credibility gap. The profile says 120 USD per hour while every visible hourly contract is 25 to 30 USD per hour.
problem.fix: Lead with fixed-price packages, where the hourly history is not the comparison point. Set the profile rate to about 85 USD per hour and bid 60 to 100 USD per hour on hourly jobs until three or more contracts at the new level are visible. This rate advice is my recommendation based on the posted ranges in market_evidence, where premium Claude jobs cluster at 30 to 80 USD per hour with a few at 50 to 200.

problem.what: The title contains none of the words buyers type. Clients search "Claude", "Claude Code", "AI agent", "n8n", "automation".
problem.fix: Use the title in the positioning section.

problem.what: Two of three catalog projects are built on OpenClaw, which has almost no demand on Upwork.
problem.fix: Replace them with the catalog projects in the offer_ladder section. Keep one OpenClaw/Hermes mention in the skills list for the few jobs that exist.

problem.what: Overview claims that a careful client can test and that may not hold up: "over 8 years of deep technical experience" sits next to a degree dated 2017 to 2021 and employment starting 2020; "100% GxP/HIPAA compliance" is a guarantee no freelancer can give.
problem.fix: State only what the profile itself can back up. Replace guarantees with specifics: what you built, for whom, with what result.

problem.what: The overview opens by challenging the reader ("are you just wasting money...") and lists four unrelated service lines.
problem.fix: Open with the outcome for one buyer type. One profile, one promise. Use a specialized profile for the second line of work.

problem.what: Portfolio shows 2023 chatbots. Nothing shows Claude, agents, skills or MCP work.
problem.fix: Add three case studies in week one (see seven_day_launch day 2). The Upwork MCP documentation in this repository is one of them.

problem.what: The 3.8-rated contract is the largest visible job. It ended April 2024, so it is now outside the 24-month Job Success window, but clients still see it.
problem.fix: Check your Top Rated perks page for the feedback-removal option and use it on this contract if you are eligible. Verify eligibility on Upwork; I did not confirm it.

problem.what: Missing skills tags: Claude Code, AI Agent Development, Model Context Protocol, n8n, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, AI Consulting, Automation.
problem.fix: Add the ones Upwork's skill list accepts and drop generic ones (Systems Engineering, Gemini) to make room.

project_catalog_data.pattern: Top listings start at 99 to 150 USD with 1 to 3 day delivery, from sellers showing 100 to 1,200+ reviews. Titles are generic ("Claude AI Developer | Claude API | Claude Code").
project_catalog_data.implication: You cannot win the catalog on price or review count. Win it with a specific outcome for a specific buyer, priced above the 99 USD crowd.

external_evidence.point: Upwork In-Demand Skills 2026: demand for skills that explicitly mention AI grew 109% year over year, against 23% for all other skills. AI integration grew 178%; AI chatbot development grew 71%.
Upwork launched its MCP server on 2026-08-10. It is free for all users, works with Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor, and every action that changes something needs user confirmation.
Agency pricing benchmark from 48 agencies that publish prices: a single workflow starts around 1,000 USD, a multi-workflow project around 3,556 USD, an ongoing retainer around 1,423 USD per month.

SKILL.md marketplaces, Q1 to Q2 2026: top skills earn roughly 500 to 3,000 USD per month, the median listed skill earns under 50 USD per month, and most revenue sits in the top 10% of listings. Typical price 5 to 25 USD per skill. Sellers that do well encode specific opinions and workflows; simple prompt wrappers do poorly.

Gumroad: revenue is extremely top-heavy. The top 1% of products take about 77% of revenue. One curated n8n template pack raised its price from 15 to 100 USD after 194 sales; a bare 8,000-template pack at about 10 USD shows 311 sales.
Skills bundles on the market today are priced from 9 to 167 USD.

verdict.supported: Demand for Claude implementation work on Upwork is real, growing and visible daily. Buyers with large Upwork spend are posting it.
Small and mid-size done-for-you engagements (1,000 to 7,500 USD) match both the Upwork postings and the outside pricing benchmarks.
verdict.not_supported: Nothing I found supports a DIY pack earning large sums quickly without an existing audience.
Very high-ticket work (15K+ USD) exists on Upwork but draws 50+ proposals fast. Expect it to come from expanding existing clients, not from cold proposals.

positioning.core_promise: I set up Claude so your team uses it every day: connected to your tools, with custom skills for your workflows, documented and handed over.

target_buyers.basis: my reading of a small sample of live postings; test and adjust
target_buyers.buyer: Professional-services firms: accounting and finance firms, agencies (marketing, SEO, recruiting), law firms.
Founders who built something with Claude Code and need review, hardening or coaching.
Operations leads who bought Claude Team/Cowork seats and are not getting value from them.

positioning.new_title: Claude AI Implementation | Claude Code, Skills & MCP | AI Agents & Automation

overview_structure.line: First two lines (all a client sees in search): who you help and the outcome. Example: "I set up Claude for business teams: Claude Code, Cowork, custom skills and MCP connectors to your CRM, inbox and docs, so work that took hours runs in minutes. Top Rated, 100% Job Success."
Three packaged offers with scope and timeline (Setup Sprint, AI Operations Audit, Done-For-You Implementation).
Three proof bullets, each one a real project with a number. Use only results you can show.
How you work: fixed scope, written acceptance criteria, recorded handover, 14 days of support.
Call to action: book a consultation or send the workflow you want automated.
overview_structure.remove: The "8 years" claim unless it is accurate and you can show it; the "100% GxP/HIPAA compliance" guarantee; the opening challenge to the reader; OpenClaw as a headline.

specialized_profiles.profile: For build-heavy jobs: agents, RAG, n8n, API integration. Keeps the general profile focused on Claude implementation.
For the coaching and training postings, which showed the lowest proposal counts.

rate_strategy.rule: Profile rate about 85 USD per hour until the visible history supports more.
Prefer fixed-price packages. They remove the hourly comparison and are easier to protect with acceptance criteria.
Raise the rate after every three completed contracts at the current level.

offer_ladder.principle: One body of work, sold three ways. The DIY kit is the same set of skills, templates and documents you use to deliver the done-for-you work. Build it once.

offer.name: Claude Setup Sprint
offer.scope: Install and configure Claude Code or Cowork, connect 1 to 3 tools through MCP connectors, build 1 to 5 custom skills for the client's real workflows, one recorded training session, a written runbook.
offer.tiers: Starter 299 USD (setup + 1 skill). Standard 599 USD (setup + 3 skills + 1 connector + training). Team 1,200 USD (up to 5 users, 5 skills, 3 connectors).
offer.role: Door-opener. Fast, low dispute risk, produces 5-star outcomes quickly.
offer.evidence: Setup and connector postings appear daily (Claude Code install, Claude Code to HubSpot MCP, Claude + GA4, Claude Team + ClickUp).

offer.name: AI Operations Audit
offer.scope: Review the client's current Claude or agent setup, or a Claude Code-built app. Deliver a written findings report, a prioritized fix list, and a costed roadmap.
offer.role: Paid discovery. This is the safe first milestone before any large build.
offer.evidence: "AI Operations Auditor: Assess Our Claude-Based Business OS" (200K+ client); "Code Review & Go-Live Check for a Claude Code-Built App" (100K+ client); "OpenClaw AI Automation QA Lead: Technical Audit" (800K+ client).

offer.name: Done-For-You Claude Implementation
offer.channel: proposals, upsell from DFY1 and DFY2
offer.scope: Team rollout, security and permissions, 8 to 15 custom skills, agents for 2 to 4 core workflows, connectors to CRM, inbox, docs and accounting, documentation, training, 14 days of support.
offer.evidence: "Claude AI Implementation Expert: Team Setup, Security, AI Agents & Business Workflows" (400K+ client); agency operations configuration at 2,500 USD; outside benchmark of about 3,556 USD for a multi-workflow project (S3).

offer.name: AI Operations Care Plan
offer.scope: Fixed monthly hours for new skills, fixes, model and tool updates, and a monthly review call.
offer.role: Recurring income, and long-term relationships help the Job Success Score (S7).
offer.evidence: Outside benchmark of about 1,423 USD per month for an ongoing retainer (S3).

offer.name: Claude Coaching and Team Training
offer.price: 100 to 150 USD per hour, or 750 USD per workshop
offer.evidence: Coaching and training postings showed the lowest competition in the sample (several at 5 to 20 proposals).

product.name: Claude Business OS Kit

contents.item: 12 to 20 SKILL.md skills for business operations: inbox triage, meeting notes to CRM, proposal drafting, client reporting, invoice chasing, research briefs, content repurposing, SOP writer.
CLAUDE.md and project-instruction templates for teams.
Connector setup guides for the tools that appeared most in the job postings: HubSpot, Google Workspace, ClickUp, GoHighLevel, Zoho, QuickBooks.
A prompt library organized by role.
A setup checklist, a security and permissions guide, and short walkthrough videos.

product.pricing: Core 49 USD. Pro 149 USD (all skills + guides + videos). Pro plus a 30-minute setup call 299 USD.
product.rule_for_what_sells: Each skill must encode a specific, opinionated workflow. Generic prompt wrappers do not sell.

product.name: Upwork MCP Proposal Engine Kit
product.contents: The documentation already in this repository, turned into a product: skills for job discovery, client vetting, proposal drafting and Connects budgeting through the official Upwork MCP, with the human-confirmation step kept in.
product.audience: Freelancers and small agencies. About 20 new "Upwork bidder / profile optimization" postings per week show the need, but posters have small budgets, so sell this as a kit, not as a service.
product.compliance: Never offer to log in to or bid from someone else's Upwork account, and never sell unattended auto-bidding. Sell setup and templates for the buyer's own account with confirmation on every submission.

channels.off_upwork: Gumroad or Lemon Squeezy with a private repository, plus one SKILL.md marketplace. Promote through GitHub (free sample skills in a public repo), LinkedIn and short demo videos.
channels.on_upwork: Sell the kit only as a customized service through Project Catalog ("You will get a Claude skills pack customized for your business"). Do not paste store links into proposals, messages or the profile.
channels.hard_rule: Keep the two channels separate. A client who found you on Upwork pays through Upwork for 24 months unless the conversion fee is paid. Do not share contact details before a contract starts.

do_it_yourself.realistic_expectation: With no existing audience, plan for 0 to 300 USD per month from the kits in the first two months. The kit pays for itself by cutting done-for-you delivery time and by serving as proof in proposals.

seven_day_launch.budget: About 80 to 110 USD: Freelancer Plus (about 20 USD per month; confirm current terms on the upgrade page) and 400 to 600 extra Connects at 0.15 USD each. Typical proposals cost 16 to 20 Connects, so your current 110 covers only 5 to 7 proposals (S9).

day.task: Rewrite title, overview and skills as in positioning. Set the rate.
Answer or decline the invitation from 2026-08-31. It costs 0 Connects.
Review the 5 in-progress contracts. For any that are finished, confirm the client is happy, then ask them to close it with feedback.
Check the Top Rated perks page for feedback removal on the 3.8-rated contract.

Publish three portfolio case studies with screenshots or a short screen recording: (1) the Upwork MCP documentation and proposal engine in this repository, (2) a Claude skills and connector setup you build for your own company as a live demo, (3) your strongest agent or RAG build.
Record one 2-minute demo video of Claude running a real business workflow end to end. Reuse it in every proposal.
Replace the two OpenClaw catalog projects with Claude Setup Sprint and AI Operations Audit. Rename AI Launchpad to match the new positioning.

Message past clients who rated you 5.0 through their existing Upwork message rooms with one specific offer (the Setup Sprint). This is the highest-probability path to a contract in week one, and repeat clients help the Job Success Score.
Send 4 to 6 vetted proposals per day using the routine in mcp_operating_system. Work the 18:30 to 23:30 IST window, when US clients post.
Apply only to jobs under 15 proposals and under 24 hours old that pass the client scorecard.
Build the first 5 skills of the DIY kit in parallel. They double as delivery assets for the first Setup Sprint.

seven_day_launch.first_week_cash_reality: Upwork holds fixed-price payments for a security period after a milestone is approved (5 days under the standard schedule), and bills hourly work weekly with funds available about 10 days after the week ends. Confirm the current schedule in your Upwork payment settings. A contract signed on day 3 with a milestone approved on day 6 pays out around day 11.

targets.note: These are planning numbers to measure against. They are not forecasts backed by data.
targets.week: 25 to 30 proposals sent, 1 to 2 contracts signed, 300 to 1,500 USD contracted.
targets.month: 2 to 4 Setup Sprints, 1 to 2 Audits, 1 implementation started: 3,000 to 8,000 USD contracted.
1 to 2 care-plan retainers running, rate history visible at the new level, 6,000 to 12,000 USD per month.

checkpoints.check: After 20 proposals: if fewer than 6 were viewed, the targeting or the first two lines of the proposal are wrong. Change those first.
If proposals are viewed but get no replies: the offer or price is wrong for that job type. Test the Audit as the entry offer.
If calls happen but do not close: tighten scope and lower the size of the first milestone.
Track weekly on the My Stats page: proposals sent, viewed, interviews, hires, profile views, invites.

how_jss_works.rule: Calculated daily over 6, 12 and 24 months; the best of the three is shown.
Based on client feedback, the reasons contracts ended, higher-value projects and long-term relationships.
Jobs with higher earnings have a bigger impact.
Contracts with rate changes can have a greater impact, in either direction.
Long-term relationships can raise the score; not having them does not lower it.
Feedback from clients Upwork has flagged for poor collaboration, or suspended, does not count against you.
Private feedback counts as well as public feedback (S10). You never see the private score, so a polite 5-star public review does not guarantee a good outcome.
A score below 90% loses the Top Rated track; below 79% makes winning work hard.

job_success_protection.your_specific_risk: Your recent base is small (about 2K USD in 12 months), so the next few contracts carry most of the weight, and a large one carries the most. Do not let the first contract with a new client be a 5,000+ USD build.

client_scorecard.use: before spending Connects; every item is visible on the job page or via MCP find_jobs action=get
client_scorecard.must_pass: Client rating from freelancers 4.7 or higher, or a new client with a detailed, specific post.
Hire rate 50% or higher for clients with history.
Read the feedback this client has given other freelancers. If they regularly give 4.0 to 4.5 with complaints, skip, whatever the budget.
Average hourly rate paid is not far below your rate.
Nobody hired yet, and under 15 proposals.
client_scorecard.red_flag: Tiny budget with large scope and urgency. A live example from today: a 100 USD fixed budget to finish a full marketplace in 7 days, with "we expect perfection" and "submit your very best price".
"Best price" or "lowest bid" language, unpaid test work, requests to talk or pay outside Upwork.
Scope that cannot be written as acceptance criteria.
client_scorecard.note: A placeholder budget (5 to 100 USD) from a client with 100K+ USD spend is not a red flag by itself. Quote your real price.

contract_rules.rule: Start every new client with a small fixed milestone (Setup Sprint or Audit). Take the large build only after that milestone ends well.
Write acceptance criteria into the first message of the contract: what is delivered, how it is tested, two revision rounds.
Keep the rate fixed inside a contract. Rate changes increase that contract's weight (S7). Open a new contract for a new rate.
On hourly contracts, log time with the Upwork tracker so hourly payment protection applies.
Send a short written update at least twice a week and a recorded demo at each milestone.
Use Upwork's mid-contract feedback request on longer contracts to catch problems early.
Before closing, ask plainly: "Is there anything that would stop you rating this 10 out of 10?" Fix it, then ask the client to close the contract.
If a client is unhappy, offer a fix first. A refund does not by itself remove the outcome; read Upwork's guidance in S7 before refunding.
Do not leave finished contracts open and idle. Close them with feedback.
Keep all payment on Upwork for Upwork-sourced clients (S8).

mcp_operating_system.account_warning: The Upwork connector in this Claude session is authorized to a different Upwork account (shown as "Patrick H."), not to the Aryan P. profile. Reconnect the connector while logged in as Aryan P. before using any MCP step below. No change was made to any Upwork account while preparing this plan.

daily_routine.runs: 3 times in the evening IST window
daily_routine.step: mode=most_recent, days_posted=1, verified_payment_only=true. Then action=search with title terms "claude", "AI agent", "automation", proposals_max=15, client_hires_min=1, sort=recency.
Score each job against the client scorecard using client_record (total spent, hire rate, rating), activityStat.jobActivity (hired, offered, interviewing) and client_feedback.
Check for an existing invite or proposal to avoid error VJ-JA-10.
Draft with the proposal template below. Attach the matching portfolio item. Boost only when the preview recommends it and the job passed every must_pass item.
You read the draft, the Connects cost and the bid, then confirm. Nothing is submitted without your approval.

proposal_template.line: One sentence that restates the client's goal in their own words, using their name if the client's reviews reveal it.
One sentence of matching proof with a number, plus the demo video link from your Upwork portfolio.
The plan in three steps with a timeline.
A fixed first milestone with price (Setup Sprint or Audit).
One specific question about their setup.
proposal_template.length: Under 150 words. No list of technologies.

mcp_operating_system.connects_budget: Cap at 100 Connects per day. Stop boosting if a week of boosted proposals shows no better view rate than unboosted ones.

limits_of_this_analysis.limit: Job counts come from Upwork search on one day and are approximate. Search matches loosely and may cap results.
I read page 1 of 3 of your work history and portfolio, not all of it.
The buyer segments are inferred from a sample of roughly 150 postings.
Targets, checkpoints and the DIY revenue range are assumptions. No source proves a specific income.
Upwork fees, Connects pricing, Freelancer Plus terms, payment holds and Top Rated perks change. Confirm each on Upwork before relying on it.
